name: Morgan Sindall Group plc
executive_summary: Morgan Sindall Group is a UK-listed construction and regeneration group operating through five decentralised divisions — Partnership Housing, Mixed Use Partnerships, Fit Out, Construction and Infrastructure — with FY 2025 revenue of £5.0bn and over 8,500 employees. The quantitative screen rates the stock a **strong buy** (16/22 models, composite 76%, five factor families: cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) on P/E 11.5×, P/B 2.7×, 3.7% yield, ROE 26.1%, net-cash balance sheet and Piotroski 8/9. Primary RNS filings confirm record FY 2025 and H1 2026 earnings, a £19.1–19.5bn secured plus preferred-bidder workload, and 20% dividend growth to 158p. The valuation hook is a statistically cheap, cash-rich compounder (18% ten-year adjusted PBT CAGR per management) trading below its 200-day moving average with neutral timing. The central debate is whether cash-generative Fit Out and public-sector Construction/Infrastructure can continue to offset housing-related capital absorption, partnership losses and eventual mean reversion in Fit Out margins.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MGNS offers an unusual combination of screen-level cheapness and contractor-quality fundamentals. The name passes Graham Enterprising, earnings yield, FCF yield, Lynch PEG, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value, Earnings Quality and Financial Health — a breadth that screens rarely achieve in UK industrials.

Filings substantiate the quality-and-cheapness alignment:

- **Earnings momentum:** FY 2025 adjusted PBT £232.6m (+35% YoY) on revenue £5,019m (+10%); adjusted EPS 370.0p (+33%). H1 2026 adjusted PBT £116.1m (+21%) on revenue £2,562m (+8%) — management's "record first half."
- **Balance sheet as competitive advantage:** Year-end net cash £531m (FY 2025), £418m at 30 Jun 2026; average daily net cash £368m (FY 2025) rising to £423m (H1 2026). Management explicitly positions net cash as a bidding differentiator for long-dated public-sector frameworks and partnerships.
- **Visibility:** Secured order book £12.0bn at FY 2025 (H1 2026: £12.2bn), with preferred-bidder work of £7.1bn (£7.3bn at H1 2026) — totals £19.1bn and £19.5bn respectively.
- **Cash returns:** FY 2025 total dividend 158p (+20%, cover 2.4× within the 2.0–2.5× policy); H1 2026 interim raised 10% to 55p. FY 2025 operating cash inflow £195.9m (87% of adjusted operating profit); free cash flow £161.5m (filing-aligned; screen FCF £170.7m).

The decentralised model lets Fit Out and Construction Services fund Partnership capital through the cycle — the structural feature separating MGNS from levered pure-play contractors. Screen failures (Graham Defensive, net-net, deep value, economic moat on ROA/margins, high dividend yield quartile) reflect P/B above deep-value thresholds and cyclical sector economics, not balance-sheet distress. The strong-buy signal is new (one week at signal, neutral timing, RSI ~42, price ~6% below 200-day SMA), so the thesis supports accumulation rather than maximum immediate sizing.
financial_review:
*Primary source: RNS filing bodies. Yahoo `financials_annual.json` used only for multi-year reported net income cross-check where noted.*

**Annual — FY 2025 (year ended 31 December 2025)**  
Source: *Results for the Full Year ended 31 December 2025* (25 Feb 2026).

| Metric | FY 2025 | FY 2024 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | £5,019m | £4,546m | +10% |
| Adj operating profit | £225.7m | £162.6m | +39% |
| Adj PBT | £232.6m | £172.5m | +35% |
| Adj EPS | 370.0p | 278.8p | +33% |
| Adj operating margin | 4.5% | 3.6% | +90 bps |
| Net cash (year-end) | £531m | £492m | +£39m |
| Avg daily net cash | £368m | £374m | — |
| Total dividend | 158.0p | 131.5p | +20% |
| Secured order book | £12.0bn | £11.4bn | +5% |

Fit Out drove the year (revenue £1,784m +37%, op profit £139.9m +41%). Construction grew (revenue £1,159m +11%, op profit £37.0m +20%). Infrastructure revenue fell 11% on early framework work but margin expanded to 4.0%. Partnership Housing remained resilient (+5% revenue, +16% op profit) despite weak private housing; capital employed rose to £446m. Mixed Use Partnerships lost £5.3m as investment was front-loaded. Operating cash inflow £195.9m; net Partnership investment £124.6m; inventories up £127m.

**Interim — H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026)**  
Source: *Results for the Half Year ended 30 June 2026* (23 Jul 2026).

| Metric | H1 2026 | H1 2025 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | £2,562m | £2,370m | +8% |
| Adj PBT | £116.1m | £95.9m | +21% |
| Adj EPS | 186.1p | 153.1p | +22% |
| Net cash | £418m | £390m | +£28m |
| Interim dividend | 55.0p | 50.0p | +10% |
| Secured order book | £12.2bn | £12.0bn | +2% |

H1 operating cash outflow £10.0m (seasonal; LTM inflow £202.6m). Going concern affirmed through 23 Jul 2027 with covenant headroom; £180m undrawn facilities. Medium-term targets raised for Fit Out (£100m–£130m) and Construction (margin 3.5%–4.0%).

**Trading updates:** 12 Feb 2026 — FY 2026 ahead of expectations, Fit Out significantly above prior £80m–£100m band; 2 Oct 2025 — FY 2025 significantly ahead on Fit Out strength.

**Gaps:** No standalone H1 2025 interim body in the filings index (comparatives embedded in H1 2026 release). Companies House interim accounts indexed are dated 2021 only. Full pension note not extracted from annual report body.

*Yahoo fallback:* Reported net income £131.7m (2024), £174.9m (2025) — directionally consistent with filing trajectory.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical and housing exposure.** Private housing demand remains subdued; Partnership Housing capital employed guided to £500m–£580m in FY 2026 with ROCE below 2025 (8% at H1 vs 10% prior year). Open-market completions fell 10% (FY 2025) and 23% (H1 2026). Mixed Use Partnerships expected small FY 2026 loss.

**Working capital.** Annual report marks working capital mismanagement risk as **increased**. Inventories rose £127m FY 2025 and a further £90m in H1 2026; net working capital swung from −£104m to +£30m.

**Building safety / regulatory.** Provisions £51.8m at 30 Jun 2026; Developers Pledge obligations live; MHCLG reimbursements may start H2 2026. Contingent liabilities on bonds, guarantees and claims disclosed with insurance mitigants.

**Fit Out normalisation.** FY 2025 op profit £139.9m well above medium-term band; FY 2026 expected below 2025 — key earnings risk.

**Cyber.** Risk status **increased** in annual report despite ISO27001 and MOD certification.

**Governance (minor).** Responsible Business Committee dissolved; CFO role expanded from Apr 2026. No going-concern qualification.

**Pension gap.** No material DB risk in extracts; full pension note not available — unverified.

RiskTags: cyclical, regulatory, competitive, other

meta_reflection.observation: Filings-first order is adequate in principle for MGNS.L (62/62 bodies; period_coverage annual=10 / interim=3 / trading_update=1) and better than names with no tagged H1: a genuine 23 Jul 2026 HY body exists. It is not adequate in practice: yahoo_quarterly_cashflow sits on the ladder but is empty (TTM suppressed — expected for a UK half-year reporter, not a true hole), alternate_news and ir_presentation_metrics are absent, and the two first-class 2026 operating updates (12 Feb and 16 Apr “Trading and Outlook for 2026”, the latter a profit upgrade that moved the shares ~10%) are period=other with priority 0, ranked below empty quarterlies. Ten ‘annual’ hits include a 19 Jan 2026 Notice of Full Year Results and a 2021 CH interim is still tagged interim. The sole tagged trading_update is the stale 2 Oct 2025 “Outlook for 2025”.

The screen emits strong_buy (16/22, five families including cheapness/quality/GARP/dividend/risk) on a contractor with sub-12% margins (Moat fail), current ratio 1.23, RSI 33 and a price<50<200 downtrend, while cyclical_exposure_detected is false and every overlay is off. FCF bases disagree (£170.7m filing-aligned vs £141.5m screen_ttm) with currency=USD and divergence_flagged false. Quality/Buffett/Piotroski can pass on 26% ROE and “no dilution” while WIP/receivables balloon and Sharesave issuance is continuous. The director–worker loop is being asked to qualitatively veto a mechanically clean headline that sector-cycle, cash-conversion, and FCF-currency overlays failed to brake.

Four worker types plus a five-task cap fit annual+interim+news+screen+gap but consume the entire budget and leave no slot for the 16 Apr 2026 profit-upgrade TU, the 12 Feb TU, the 24 Mar AFR, the 14 May CH group accounts, or the 14 Aug 2026 amended CH accounts. summarize_filing_body cannot carry period=annual|interim|trading_update|amendment, and there is no type to cluster TVR/Sharesave/PDMR RNSs or parse IR slides (news cites “FY 2025 slides”). gap_inventory can only list those holes — it cannot fill them.

weeks_at_signal=1 / stability=new / conviction=0.496 already mark a fresh print, but there is no watch schema for: post-H1 Q3 trading update (typical October for this issuer; catalog fetch 2 Sep has none), FY2026 guidance vs the unread April upgrade, Fit Out concentration, housing/regeneration WIP cash lock-up, remaining Sharesave issuance vs the £4,169.88/£4,001.40 ladder, or the unread August CH amendment. RSI 33 + SMA200-flat timing=neutral is not a substitute. News freshness ends ~1 Sep; filings_index fetched 2 Sep — a two-day stall versus today (4 Sep).

A generic FINANCIAL REVIEW / RISKS split will blend statutory and adjusted contractor margins and will not force Fit Out versus Construction versus Infrastructure versus Partnership Housing / Urban Regeneration, order-book secured versus preferred, company net cash versus IFRS-16 versus restricted cash, or FCF £170.7m versus £141.5m. Without explicit SEGMENT MIX, WORKING CAPITAL / CASH CONVERSION, CAPITAL RETURNS, and GUIDANCE PATH (Feb TU → Apr upgrade → Jul H1) slots, workers will treat AD HOC NEWS “stock holds firm” syndication and Sharesave listings as colour. No required slot for reporting-currency hygiene or for ‘April TU and August amended accounts exist as unread bodies’. Director catalog pass can form these questions without drafting the memo.
